hero.subtitle: a community space working with art and sustainable practices

description.text: ConceitoArte is a community space working with art and sustainable practices in Sarandi, one of the neighbourhoods most affected by the 2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods. Their Miyawaki micro-forest is already planted and will be use to validate ApeForest's data collection, tracking and platform tools.

methodology.title: Plantation Method
methodology.text: The Miyawaki method, developed by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, is an accelerated reforestation technique that creates dense, biodiverse, and resilient native forests in small areas and in a short period of time (20 to 30 years, compared to 100 years for natural regeneration).

resilience.title: Rooted in resilience
resilience.text1: In May 2024, Rio Grande do Sul experienced the worst floods in its recorded history. Over 2.3 million people were affected and Sarandi was one of the last neighbourhoods in Porto Alegre to see the water recede.
resilience.text2: When the floodwaters finally left, they left behind damaged soil and a community in recovery. Native forests help retain water, stabilise soil and reduce the impact of future flooding — making reforestation not just an environmental act but a survival strategy.

soil.title: Soil preparation
soil.text: The area was prepared using an excavator that removed 50 cm of compacted fill soil across the entire 100 m². The removed soil was placed along the edges of the plot, forming a natural border and creating a water retention basin. Compost was then added to enrich the soil before planting.

1.description: A graceful secondary forest tree with showy white flowers and medicinal bark. Highly valued in traditional phytotherapy. Key mid-succession species in gallery forests.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds; supports mid-canopy insect diversity.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Not edible, but community foragers value bark for tea and wound treatments.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates dry periods and compacted soils; good riparian buffer in RS winters.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate growth rate with medium-density wood; reasonable long-term biomass.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Key mid-succession gap-filler; bridges pioneer and climax layers in gallery forest.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Bark widely traded for phytotherapy; economically significant for local healers.

2.description: Fast-growing nitrogen-fixing pioneer legume that rapidly colonises degraded soils. Critical for soil recovery in early succession stages.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Limited fruit appeal but flowers support generalist bees in early succession.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Toxic seeds; not edible — historically used as ichthyotoxin for fishing.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Extremely hardy on degraded, exposed sites; one of the first to stabilise bare soil.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Fast growth gives early carbon gains; wood density is moderate.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Nitrogen fixation dramatically accelerates soil recovery for following species.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Traditional fish-poison use; nursery communities can sell seedlings for restoration contracts.

3.description: Resilient pioneer with bright red berries (Brazilian pink pepper) attracting birds. Excellent for riverbank stabilisation and degraded area restoration.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Red berries attract over 40 bird species; important corvid and thrush food source.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Brazilian pink pepper — commercial spice with active market; fruit edible in moderation.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates drought, flooding, and saline soils; one of the most resilient RS natives.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Slow biomass accumulation; moderate wood density but limited stature.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Rapid coloniser of river margins; excellent for preventing erosion post-flood.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Pink pepper harvest creates direct income for Guarani and small-scale farmers.

4.description: A butterfly-flowered pioneer with orchid-like blooms, widely used in folk medicine for diabetes management. Tolerates poor soils and urban conditions.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Large white flowers are prime nectar source for hawk-moths and nocturnal pollinators.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Leaves used in medicinal teas; no significant edible food value for communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Thrives on compacted, nutrient-poor urban soils; tolerates seasonal drought.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate growth rate; wood is light and carbon gains are limited in short lifespan.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Useful pioneer but shallow-rooted; succession value lower than legume pioneers.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Leaves sold fresh and dried for diabetes management — high demand in herbal markets.

5.description: Aromatic fruiting tree producing sweet fragrant fruits that attract mammals and birds. Important food sovereignty tree for Guarani communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Fruit consumed by tapirs, peccaries, toucans, and over 30 bird species.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Sweet aromatic fruit eaten fresh and used in juices, jams and artisanal liqueurs.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Handles RS frost and seasonal drought; moderately resilient across the state.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Medium-density wood and moderate growth; solid mid-range carbon contribution.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Critical mid-succession species bridging open habitat and closed-canopy forest.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Central to Guarani food culture; fruit harvest generates seasonal income for families.

6.description: Yellow-fruited native guava producing sweet vitamin-rich fruit multiple times a year. Highly productive understory tree supporting birds and small mammals.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Year-round fruiting sustains birds and small mammals even in forest lean seasons.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Sweet yellow fruit with very high vitamin C; eaten fresh, in jams and fermented drinks.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS frosts and light drought; adapts well to forest edge conditions.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Small stature and short lifespan limit biomass accumulation.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Important understorey layer but limited structural role in canopy succession.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Fruit harvested for home use and small-scale sale at local markets year-round.

7.description: Iconic purple-flowering climax tree and national symbol of Brazil. Exceptional timber and carbon value. Flowers before leafing, providing crucial early-season nectar for bees.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Pre-leaf flowering provides the first major nectar flush of the season for bees and hummingbirds.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; inner bark has traditional medicinal use as anti-inflammatory.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Deep taproot tolerates drought; deciduous habit allows survival of RS dry winters.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Dense hardwood, slow growth over 80–100 years accumulates exceptional biomass.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Dominant canopy climax species; defines mature Atlantic Forest structure and longevity.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Premium timber species and cultural icon; seedlings in high demand for restoration.

8.description: Valuable timber species producing lightweight durable wood used in carpentry. Small white flowers attract bees and insects. Important secondary canopy contributor.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: White flowers attract generalist bees; limited fruit value for wildlife.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No significant edible use; not part of indigenous food systems.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Adapts to varied RS soils; semi-deciduous allowing frost tolerance.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Good wood density and tall stature; significant long-term carbon storage.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Useful secondary canopy species but not a biodiversity anchor on its own.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Highly valued lightweight timber used in furniture, doors and traditional boats.

9.description: Tall leguminous tree fixing atmospheric nitrogen while producing dense durable timber. Simultaneously improves soils, sequesters high carbon, and supports canopy biodiversity.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Flowers attract bees and beetles; canopy supports epiphytic orchids and bromeliads.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Bark used medicinally; seeds not edible. No food value for communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Deep roots and nitrogen fixation help it establish in degraded, nutrient-poor soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Very dense wood combined with tall stature makes it a top carbon sequesterer in RS.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Dual role as N-fixer and canopy species makes it exceptionally valuable in restoration design.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Bark tannins used in leather treatment; dense timber valued for heavy construction.

10.description: Medium-to-large tree with fibrous bark traditionally used for rope-making. Flowers attract numerous pollinators. Excellent riparian species tolerating periodic flooding.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Abundant flowers attract diverse bees, wasps and beetles across an extended bloom season.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; bark fibre used for cordage but not food.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: One of few medium trees that tolerates both seasonal flooding and dry spells in RS.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Medium density timber with good stature; solid carbon contribution over 50+ years.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Critical for riparian corridor restoration after 2024-type flood events in RS.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Inner bark fibre used for rope and traditional weaving; anti-inflammatory folk medicine.

11.description: Mid-succession understory tree with fragrant white flowers rich in nectar. Bark has traditional medicinal uses. Valuable for understorey biodiversity development.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Highly fragrant flowers are a rare and important nectar source for specialist bees.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Bark has folk anti-rheumatic use; not a food plant.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Handles seasonal moisture variability; grows in both humid and drier RS sites.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Modest stature and wood density; carbon role is limited but cumulative in dense plantings.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Fills critical understorey layer, providing shade and humidity for seedling establishment.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Bark used in traditional medicine for joint pain; moderate local knowledge value.

12.description: Red-fruited native guava — one of the most productive and wildlife-important small trees in the Atlantic Forest. Fruits year-round, supporting birds, mammals and communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Continuous year-round fruiting supports birds, bats and small mammals even in dry season.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Abundant sweet-tart fruit eaten fresh, in jams, juices and wine; multiple harvests yearly.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Hardy across RS conditions including light frost; tolerates both wet and dry soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Small shrub-like stature limits carbon storage despite long productive lifespan.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Reliable food source sustains frugivores year-round, amplifying seed dispersal across the site.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Highest-use food plant for Guarani — fresh fruit, beverages and preserved goods sold locally.

13.description: Spectacular yellow-flowering legume with nitrogen-fixing roots. Dense canopy provides excellent shade and timber. One of the most important large secondary forest trees in southern Brazil.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Abundant yellow flowers are key dry-season nectar source; pods feed seed-eating birds.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; pods are ornamental rather than edible.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates heavy RS summer rains and moderate winter frosts; hardy on disturbed soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Reaches 25m with dense wood; among the highest carbon values of secondary RS trees.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Nitrogen fixation plus tall canopy: rare dual-function species accelerating succession.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Valued timber for construction; fast enough growth for community forestry rotation.

14.description: Aromatic laurel-family climax tree producing small black fruits vital for frugivorous birds. Bark used as spice in regional cuisine. Anchors mature forest biodiversity.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Small lipid-rich black fruits are critical food for toucans, cotingas and migratory birds.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Aromatic bark used as cinnamon substitute in regional cooking; bark oil traded locally.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Evergreen canopy handles RS winter frosts; shade tolerance enables understorey regeneration.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Dense laurel-family wood persisting 60–100 years accumulates solid long-term carbon.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Dominant climax species in mixed ombrophilous forest; defines mature forest microclimate.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Bark harvested for spice and folk medicine; timber used in fine carpentry.

15.description: Native custard-apple bearing large edible fruit highly nutritious for communities and wildlife. Particularly important for tapirs and large mammals. Strong food sovereignty value for Guarani.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Large fruits consumed by tapirs, peccaries and woolly monkeys — key megafauna food.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Custard-like sweet flesh eaten fresh; high caloric and nutritional value for communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Adapted to RS summer heat; less frost-tolerant but survives typical RS winters.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Modest stature and wood density; carbon contribution is moderate.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Large seed size means dispersal depends on megafauna, making it a restoration indicator species.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: One of the most culturally important fruits for Guarani; traded at indigenous food fairs.

16.description: Valued timber tree with creamy white flowers attracting abundant pollinators. Wood used for furniture and construction. Combines high timber value with pollinator support.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Prolific white flowers attract large bee guilds; canopy supports cavity-nesting birds.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No significant edible value; timber species only.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates varied RS soils; semi-deciduous reducing frost stress in winter.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate-to-high density wood in a tall secondary tree; solid carbon sequestration.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Important structural canopy species accelerating closed-forest formation at this site.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: High-quality furniture and construction timber; active local demand for Guajuvira wood.

17.description: Native jacaranda producing blue-purple flowers rich in nectar. Bark used medicinally for skin conditions. Provides mid-canopy biodiversity layer.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Blue tubular flowers are specialist resource for long-tongued bees and hummingbirds.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; bark extract used topically for skin conditions only.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS frosts and variable rainfall; robust across forest edge to interior.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Medium-density wood; contributes moderate carbon at mid-canopy heights.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Creates visual and structural complexity in the forest mid-layer; supports epiphytes.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Bark decoctions used for syphilis and skin infections in traditional medicine.

18.description: Golden-flowering climax tree — Brazil's national flower. Provides critical early-spring nectar. Dense durable timber and exceptional long-term carbon storage.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Mass golden flowering before leaf flush is the most important early-spring bee event in RS forest.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; bark has minor traditional anti-inflammatory use.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Deciduous strategy conserves moisture; deep roots handle RS drought and winter frosts.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Very dense hardwood accumulating over 80–100 years; exceptional lifetime carbon storage.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Canopy climax anchor; defines mature Atlantic Forest physiognomy in southern Brazil.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Brazil's national flower symbol; premium timber; high seedling demand for restoration.

19.description: Native wild peach with sweet edible fruit beloved by birds and communities. Prolific fruiter supporting birds and small mammals year-round in riparian and secondary forest environments.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Prolific fruiting supports thrushes, tanagers and small mammals across extended seasons.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Sweet peach-flavoured fruit eaten fresh and used in jams and artisanal spirits.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS flooding, frost and seasonal drought — versatile across the state.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Small stature and moderate wood density; limited individual carbon contribution.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Riparian understorey specialist; crucial for riverbank biodiversity recovery after floods.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Fruit widely used in home kitchens and sold at community markets; easy to propagate.

20.description: Tall climax forest tree with distinctive dark-winged seeds. Excellent dense timber and high long-term carbon storage. An important but uncommon mature canopy species.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Winged seeds dispersed by wind; limited direct wildlife food value but canopy supports epiphytes.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible or widely used medicinal parts; timber species only.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Established in RS climax forests; handles typical seasonal variation once established.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Very dense wood in a large canopy tree persisting 100 years; excellent carbon sink.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Rare climax component whose inclusion increases long-term forest resilience and authenticity.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: High-value dense timber; presence signals mature forest quality to conservation assessors.

21.description: Large-leaved fig tree — a true keystone species. Continuous fruiting across all seasons makes it perhaps the single most important biodiversity tree in the entire planting.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Figs support over 1,200 vertebrate species globally; continuous fruiting sustains year-round biodiversity.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Abundant small figs consumed by birds, bats, primates and communities; processed into preserves.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Extensive root system stabilises soils; canopy creates microclimate buffering heat and drought.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Reaches 30m with massive trunk; one of the highest lifetime carbon stores in the Atlantic Forest.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Absolute keystone; no other species can substitute its role as continuous multi-season food source.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Sacred tree in many indigenous cultures; fruit edible and timber used in traditional construction.

22.description: Smaller-leaved native fig sharing keystone status with its larger relative at a more accessible canopy height. Excellent complement in layered planting design.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Dense fruiting sustains understorey wildlife; important for smaller birds unable to reach large figs.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Small figs consumed by birds, bats and communities; used in traditional preserves.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Adapts to RS seasonality; aggressive root system handles both wet and dry periods.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Dense wood with 80–100yr lifespan; strong individual carbon contribution at mid-canopy.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Provides continuous food at lower canopy height, complementing the large-leaved fig perfectly.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Cultural significance shared with all native figs; fruit used locally; important for agroforestry.

23.description: Prolific-fruiting small tree producing clusters of red berries extremely attractive to birds. One of the most important bird-food plants in southern Brazilian forests.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Dense red berry clusters attract over 50 bird species; among top 3 bird-food trees in RS.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Small berries edible and used in artisanal wine and fermentation by communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Fast establishment on degraded soils; tolerates RS frost and periodic waterlogging.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Small stature and short lifespan; carbon role is local and cumulative rather than individual.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Fast growth and prolific fruiting rapidly restores bird-plant interaction networks at degraded sites.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Berries used in folk wine; fast-growing species easy to produce in community nurseries.

24.description: Iconic Brazilian trunk-fruiting tree producing sweet grape-like fruits directly on the bark. Fruits multiple times a year, supporting pollinators and frugivores.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Trunk-borne flowers attract pollinators directly; fruit consumed by bats, birds and mammals.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Sweet grape-flavoured fruit eaten fresh, fermented into wine and liqueur; multiple harvests yearly.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Thrives in tropical-subtropical RS climate; resilient to heat and moderate drought.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate growth rate and lifespan; reasonable carbon contribution for its size.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Understorey species with limited canopy role; most value is food network rather than structure.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Cultural icon of Brazilian agroforestry; jaboticaba wine is a commercially significant product.

25.description: Silver-leafed pioneer shrub-tree with abundant small red fruits important for birds. Critical coloniser of degraded Pampa grasslands, enabling forest-savanna transition.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Small red fruits attract resident birds; silver foliage provides microhabitat for insects.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Fruits not commonly eaten by communities; limited food sovereignty value.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Pioneer of open degraded Pampa — extremely tough; survives exposure, drought and poor soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Shrub-like stature and short lifespan severely limit carbon accumulation.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: First woody species to colonise degraded Pampa grassland, enabling forest succession to begin.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Limited community use; value lies in its ecological role rather than direct human benefit.

26.description: Fast-growing pioneer tolerating flooding and waterlogged soils, essential for riparian restoration. The first trees to re-establish gallery forest and floodplains after flood events.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Supports aquatic insects and riparian birds; limited fruit value for wildlife.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible use; not part of community food systems.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Survives complete inundation; the defining RS flood-resilience pioneer after 2024-type events.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate wood density; fast growth provides early carbon gains in riparian corridors.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Irreplaceable for floodplain restoration; nothing else matches its flood tolerance in RS.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Limited direct use but essential for protecting farmland and indigenous land from floods.

27.description: Named after the toucan — produces aromatic fruits heavily consumed by toucans and tanagers. Excellent nectar source for bees. Effective for restoring forest-bird communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Aromatic fruits attract toucans, tanagers and thrushes — key indicator species for forest recovery.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Fruits not significant for human consumption; ecological food value far exceeds community use.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS seasonal drought and light frost; hardy on degraded soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate stature and wood density; moderate carbon contribution over 30–50yr.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Presence of toucans feeding here signals successful restoration of forest bird community.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Aromatic fruit used in folk medicine; trees easily propagated in local nurseries.

28.description: The great Atlantic Forest cedar — majestic, valuable timber and the highest individual carbon sequesterer in this planting. Threatened by shoot borer; mixed plantings reduce vulnerability.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Large hollow trunks provide nesting for raptors; canopy supports epiphytic communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible use; resin has minor traditional medicinal application.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Adapted to RS climate but vulnerable to shoot borer in monocultures; mixed plantings essential.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Reaches 35m with very dense aromatic wood; highest individual carbon value in the planting.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Keystone canopy giant whose threatened status makes each planted individual conservation critical.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Most prized cabinet timber in South America; significant economic value for community forestry.

29.description: Nitrogen-fixing pioneer shrub with spectacular pink powder-puff flowers. Outstanding hummingbird and bee forage. Rapidly covers degraded soil, enabling succession.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Pink powder-puff flowers are primary hummingbird and bee forage on the degraded site.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: No edible parts; value is entirely ecological. Flowers are ornamentally significant.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Dense root system prevents erosion; nitrogen fixation enriches bare soils immediately.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Shrub stature and short lifespan severely limit individual carbon sequestration.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: First nitrogen-fixer to stabilise bare soil; creates conditions for all subsequent succession.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Seedlings easily sold by community nurseries; attractive for urban gardens and restoration.

30.description: Native wild cherry producing abundant sweet cherries relished by birds and communities. Fruit used in jams, liqueurs and fresh consumption by local communities.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Cherry-red fruits attract thrushes, tanagers and mammals; flowers support native bees.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Sweet cherry flavour excellent fresh; prime ingredient for artisanal jams and liqueurs.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS frosts and seasonal drought; resilient across varied southern forest habitats.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate-density wood in a mid-sized tree; reasonable but not outstanding carbon storage.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Important secondary understorey species supporting frugivore communities year-round.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Cherry liqueur and jam production is an active income stream for RS indigenous communities.

31.description: Highland native feijoa producing distinctive aromatic fruit with sweet white flesh. Frost-tolerant — exceptional climate resilience for Rio Grande do Sul winters.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Thick petals eaten by birds directly off the flower; fruit consumed by multiple species.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Highly aromatic guava-like flesh; eaten fresh or in premium jams; growing export market.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Native to RS highlands; the most frost-tolerant fruiting species in this entire planting.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Small shrub-tree stature; carbon contribution modest but lifespan gives cumulative gains.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Important in highland Atlantic Forest edges; limited role in lowland succession contexts.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Feijoa is increasingly exported and fetches premium prices; strong commercial opportunity.

32.description: The Surinam cherry — one of Brazil's most beloved native fruits. Produces abundant red-to-black fruit rich in vitamins C and A, attracting birds and humans alike.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Abundant fruit consumed by many bird species; flowers attract native bees year-round.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Exceptional vitamin C and A content; eaten fresh, in juices and frozen treats; beloved across Brazil.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Adapted across RS from coast to highlands; tolerates frost and moderate drought.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Variable stature; carbon role limited but the 2 individuals still contribute to site diversity.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Important understorey fruiting species; limited canopy structure role at small individual count.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Most culturally significant native fruit for Guarani; pitanga juice is a commercial community product.

33.description: Small to medium tree producing abundant dark berries critical for tanagers and thrushes. Supports bird-mediated seed dispersal, amplifying overall restoration effectiveness.

ecologicalScores.label: Biodiversity
ecologicalScores.description: Dark berries are primary food for tanagers and thrushes — seed dispersal multiplier species.

ecologicalScores.label: Food Security
ecologicalScores.description: Berries not eaten by communities; limited direct food value beyond wildlife.

ecologicalScores.label: Climate Resilience
ecologicalScores.description: Tolerates RS seasonal variation; grows well on rocky or nutrient-poor soils.

ecologicalScores.label: Carbon Sequestration
ecologicalScores.description: Moderate wood density and mid-sized stature; reasonable individual carbon contribution.

ecologicalScores.label: Ecological Role
ecologicalScores.description: Bird-dispersed seeds from this tree travel far, seeding new areas and amplifying restoration reach.

ecologicalScores.label: Community Benefit
ecologicalScores.description: Limited direct use; value is ecological. Easy to propagate for community nursery sales.
